name: Mesocardia

criteria.description: Heart apex located at the midline of the thorax on imaging
No evidence of dextrocardia or situs inversus
Presence or absence of associated congenital heart defects

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of heart apex located at midline on imaging without dextrocardia or situs inversus
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Mesocardia is a positional anomaly and may be isolated or associated with other cardiac malformations.

pathognomonic.notes: Palpable apex beat located at the midline of the chest
searchTerms: heart apex beat felt in middle of chest

pathognomonic.symptomName: Central cardiac silhouette on chest radiograph
pathognomonic.notes: Heart shadow centered in the thorax without lateral displacement
searchTerms: heart shadow centered on chest X-ray

common.symptomName: Murmur due to associated congenital heart defect
common.notes: Often detected if mesocardia coexists with structural anomalies
searchTerms: abnormal heart sound due to congenital defect

common.notes: May occur if associated cardiac defects impair pulmonary circulation
Observed if intracardiac shunts are present
searchTerms: cyanosis due to cardiac blood mixing

occasional.notes: May be reported in older children or adults
Due to compromised cardiac function if associated defects exist
Secondary to cardiac anomalies affecting pulmonary circulation

rare.notes: Occurs if severe associated cardiac defects are present
May result from arrhythmias or poor cardiac output

imaging: Chest X-ray showing midline cardiac silhouette
Echocardiography confirming cardiac apex position and assessing associated defects
Cardiac MRI for detailed anatomical evaluation
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; may be sporadic or associated with syndromic conditions
other: Physical examination revealing midline apical impulse
Electrocardiogram may be normal or show changes related to associated defects

distinguishingFeatures: Heart apex located on the right side of the thorax
Mirror-image reversal of thoracic and abdominal organs
Heart apex typically on right side

redFlags: Recurrent respiratory infections with failure to thrive
references: Moss and Adams' Heart Disease in Infants, Children, and Adolescents, 9th Edition
UpToDate: Congenital malpositions of the heart
